decisions.reason: Attributes the single crash to plugin A's unconditional useSessionPendingInteraction call at client.js:219:41, walks the contract diff showing the hook removed and replaced by useSessionStatus with useSessions retained, and establishes B consumes no standard-kit hooks and never threw.

Uses dock-render-tree.md to show the whole input.dock list shares one DrawerErrorBoundary (no per-entry boundary), so A's throw nulls the entire subtree including B's chips, while input.left's independent boundary keeps the attach button; cites the boundary-fallback console line listing both unmounted entries.

Treats the A-disable experiment as closing the causal chain (A's crash unmounts the slot; B renders when freed) while explicitly denying it proves B's full alpha.2 compatibility or that A's crash is the only dock defect; reinstalling B is shown to be inert, and the colleague theory refuted.

Corrected adapter-based component reads pending via useSessionStatus(...).pendingInteraction on alpha.2, falls back to the legacy hook, and degrades to a stable no-attention shape when neither exists, never calling a missing seat; explains silent degradation because a throwing dock tenant unmounts co-tenants while a missing indicator is cosmetic.

No-host-restart verification via rebuilt client bundle and hard refresh with both entries mounted; B-specific regression covering paste/drop/remove and coexistence with A enabled; hygiene covers defensive kit probing, per-entry tenant boundary, and host per-entry boundaries with an explicit isolation-vs-fail-loudness trade-off.

caps.reason: The fix targets plugin A only; reinstalling B and the independent-two-bugs framing are explicitly rejected.
